messages:
jess: Heads up — after last night's key rotation one of the production Lambdas started failing with AccessDenied on kms:Decrypt when invoked via the cross-account role. Not seeing obvious policy denials in IAM. Anyone seen the grant/rotation combo bite us like this?

sam: Can you paste the CloudTrail Decrypt event and the assumed role ARN? also which key (alias/arn)

jess: CloudTrail snippet (redacted):
```
{
  "eventName": "Decrypt",
  "eventTime": "2026-03-19T22:10:03Z",
  "errorCode": "AccessDeniedException",
  "userIdentity": {
    "type": "AssumedRole",
    "arn": "arn:aws:sts::999999999999:assumed-role/crossacct-lambda-role/session-123"
  },
  "requestParameters": {
    "keyId": "arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:111111111111:key/abcd-ef01-2345",
    "encryptionContext": {
      "lambda:aws:arn": "arn:aws:lambda:us-east-1:111111111111:function:proc-enc"
    }
  }
}
```

marie: A few things to check quickly: 1) key policy principals vs the assumed-role principal (cross-account nuance), 2) any existing KMS grants (grants created pre-rotation might reference the old principal name), 3) encryptionContext conditions in the key policy. Also confirm whether the Lambda is using a grant token.

dinesh: Quick commands that have helped before:
```bash
aws kms list-grants --key-id arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:111111111111:key/abcd-ef01-2345 --profile security
aws kms get-key-policy --key-id alias/prod-data-key --policy-name default --profile security
aws iam get-role --role-name crossacct-lambda-role --profile crossacct
```

jess: Ran list-grants — it shows two grants but both principal ARNs reference the old role name (crossacct-lambda-role-v1). We rotated role names during a deployment and the new assumed-role is crossacct-lambda-role (no -v1).

sam: That explains it — grants are principal-specific. When you change the role name the existing grants no longer match the principal making the Decrypt call, so KMS denies unless the role is in the key policy. If the key policy allowed the account root or the KMS service principal, it might have still worked, but looks like we relied on grants.

marie: Two remediation paths: 1) Create a new grant for the new assumed-role ARN (aws kms create-grant ... --grantee-principal arn:aws:sts::999999999999:assumed-role/crossacct-lambda-role/session) OR 2) Update key policy to reference the IAM role principal (preferred long-term: use role ARN without depending on ephemeral grant tokens). Note: grants created by services (e.g., for Lambda) can be ephemeral or tied to older role naming.

dinesh: Also double-check encryptionContext requirement — if the key policy has a Condition on encryptionContext values the Decrypt will fail even if the principal matches. CloudTrail shows an encryptionContext; confirm policy conditions.

deploy-bot: :rotating_light: key-rotation event recorded: key/abcd-ef01-2345 rotated (versionId=9f3b). Triggered by infra/rotation-job at 2026-03-19T03:00:00Z.

jess: Action items: (1) create a temporary grant for the new role so prod is unblocked, (2) update key policy to include the IAM role principal and account, (3) add a post-rotation checklist to the rotation job to run list-grants -> reconcile principals. I'll create a PR to add the role ARN to the key policy and open a quick runbook for rotation.

sam: +1. If someone creates the grant, include a note to expire it (CreateGrant with RetireOn). I'll pick this up if jess is tied up. :thumbsup:

marie: Also add a check in deploy pipeline to avoid renaming roles in a way that breaks existing grants, or create a stable role alias pattern.

jess: Thanks — will follow up with PR and rollout steps.
